tasks.short: Prepare, authorize, dispatch and reconcile occasional cheque payments.

steps.what: Retrieve approved invoices due for payment from the {ERP}.
Check amounts, payees and addresses against invoices and supplier records.
Generate and print cheques and remittance slips from the {ERP}.
Review supporting invoices and sign the cheque batch.
Match signed cheques to remittances, seal envelopes and dispatch post.
Match cleared cheques against the payment register and flag outstanding items.

tasks.design: For recipients accepting electronic payment, configure the {ERP} to create transfer batches using independently verified bank details and reconcile confirmations from the {BANK}. A finance signatory approves release in the {BANK}; the {ERP} sends remittances through the {EMAIL}, removing printing and posting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legacy payment habits, missing verified bank details and separated payment permissions kept physical handling in place.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing payment exports, bank imports and reconciliation rules usually supply the core capability. Assisted coding can reduce the cost of any missing connector.
tasks.still_hard: Fraudulent bank-detail changes, rejected transfers and recipients requiring cheques still need attention. Payment release requires segregation of duties.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize suspicious changes, resolve disputed amounts and decide whether a payment should proceed.

ambition.what: Review unresolved payment exceptions each working day.

tasks.altitude: Postal preparation gives way to a short payment-exception review. The assistant can investigate discrepancies; payment approval rights remain with finance.

reach.task: Review administrative payment controls and exception causes.
reach.learn: Bank reconciliation, supplier verification and segregation of duties.

evidence.claim: Electronic payment batches and rule-based reconciliation are established finance capabilities; local support needs confirmation.
Cheque handling is generally a residual process in mid-size European companies, with substantial variation.

assumptions: Today's steps describe the residual cheque process where this task still exists, rather than the dominant European payment method.
The future step ratings apply to recipients who accept electronic payment; mandatory cheque exceptions retain physical handling.
Verified bank details already exist or are obtained through a separate controlled process.
The finance signatory's time is included in the task shares.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one payment entity and one bank connection, not measured savings.
unknowns: Actual cheque volume and reasons electronic payment is unavailable.
Available payment formats, bank interfaces and reconciliation features.
Who can maintain payee details, create batches and release payments.
Whether local access or employee consultation requirements affect rollout.
research_questions: Which recipient categories can move to electronic payment without changing contractual terms?
What duplicate-payment and replay controls does the payment interface provide?
new_work: Verify new bank details through an independent channel.
Resolve rejected transfers and unmatched bank entries.
Maintain approval limits, connector credentials and audit records.

tasks.short: Arrange meetings, conferences and travel within staff preferences, availability and budget.

steps.what: Collect dates, destinations, attendee needs and budget through the {EMAIL}.
Check attendee availability and meeting rooms in the {CALENDAR}.
Compare transport, accommodation and venue offers in the travel booking system {OTHER}.
Agree an itinerary and resolve preference or policy conflicts through the {EMAIL}.
Obtain budget approval and purchase reservations in the travel booking system {OTHER}.
Send confirmations and add the itinerary to the {CALENDAR}.
Resolve cancellations, disruptions or changed needs with the traveller and supplier.

tasks.design: A structured form in the {WORKFLOW} collects requirements and checks the {CALENDAR}; supported interfaces to the travel booking system {OTHER} return live, policy-filtered options. The traveller chooses, a budget holder approves purchase, and configured booking flows distribute confirmations through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. The administrative assistant handles unusual arrangements and disruptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preferences arrived in incomplete messages, and availability, prices and approvals sat in separate places.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake and existing booking rules remove much of the coordination. Small integrations are cheaper to implement and validate with assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Prices change before purchase, supplier interfaces vary, and accessibility or disruption needs require conversation. Savings depend on the booking channels actually available.
tasks.human_edge: Balance convenience, accessibility, cost and relationships when a policy-compliant option still fails the traveller.

ambition.what: Offer a pre-departure itinerary and accessibility check for first-time business travellers.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time chasing details and copying confirmations, and more time resolving difficult arrangements. Booking and spending limits remain delegated by the budget holder.

reach.task: Compare travel suppliers and recurring booking problems.
reach.learn: Cancellation terms, accessibility requirements and total trip cost.

evidence.claim: Turning a mail thread into a meeting invitation and agenda is available today; this does not establish travel-purchase automation.
The departmental evaluation found scheduling took longer on average, so local timing must establish any benefit.
Structured booking forms, calendar rules and policy filters can automate routine coordination without a model.

assumptions: The task combines meeting-only requests and occasional travel; travel purchases apply only to the latter.
The target uses supported booking features rather than unattended navigation across arbitrary supplier websites.
Routine requests move to structured intake; unusual requests remain with a person.
The purchase gate applies to the final price and cancellation terms, with renewed approval outside agreed limits.
Sensitive accessibility information is minimized and access restricted under GDPR.
Build ranges assume one booking channel; they are estimates rather than demonstrated delivery times.
unknowns: Existing booking channels, supported interfaces and purchase permissions.
Share of requests requiring travel, external venues or policy exceptions.
Approval thresholds and acceptable price changes before purchase.
Calendar visibility and handling rules for sensitive traveller needs.
research_questions: Can the booking channel hold a price while approval is pending?
Which cancellation and rebooking operations are supported reliably?
new_work: Maintain booking policies, approval limits and intake fields.
Review stale prices, failed reservations and duplicate-booking alerts.
Check access to traveller details and remove unnecessary sensitive data.
Measure completion time and correction rates against the current process.

tasks.short: Supervise clerical work and orient, train and support new administrative staff.

steps.what: Review open assignments, deadlines and coverage in the {PROJECT}.
Agree assignments and resolve workload conflicts with clerical staff.
Assemble role instructions, contacts and an orientation checklist from the {DOCS}.
Welcome new staff and demonstrate office procedures and tools.
Observe practice tasks, correct errors and judge readiness for independent work.
Record orientation completion and schedule outstanding learning in the {LMS}.
Discuss progress, confidence and further support with each staff member.

tasks.design: Configure a shared workload view in the {PROJECT} and generate orientation packs from approved, versioned procedures in the {DOCS}. The clerical supervisor assigns work, teaches and confirms readiness; those confirmations update the {LMS} and trigger follow-up reminders through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orientation material was assembled repeatedly, and assignment and learning records were disconnected. The relational work itself was never a good automation target.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates, task views and learning triggers already exist. Assisted coding makes a small document assembler and connector more affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Recognizing confusion, building confidence, judging readiness and distributing work fairly require contextual knowledge and trust.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unspoken difficulties, adapt teaching and handle disagreements without reducing people to completion scores.

ambition.what: Provide a first-month practice clinic for new clerical staff across departments.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time assembling packs and updating records, leaving more room for observed practice and individual coaching. Existing assignment and readiness decisions remain human; new employment decision rights are not implied.

reach.task: Design cross-department clerical induction and service coverage.
reach.learn: Instructional design, accessible training and fair workload planning.

evidence.claim: Role-based document assembly and completion-triggered learning records are conventional deterministic capabilities.
AI used for staff task allocation or monitoring may fall within Annex III point 4; AI literacy duties also apply.
Employee-data access, purpose limitation and consultation under applicable national rules need local assessment.

assumptions: This responsibility is held by a lead assistant or clerical supervisor, rather than every administrative assistant.
The workload view summarizes existing assignments and deadlines; it does not score staff or allocate work using AI.
The generated pack assembles approved material without inventing procedures.
Completion records reflect explicit human confirmations, not inferred competence.
GDPR applies to employee records; consultation depends on national rules and the actual change.
Build ranges include access and possible consultation effort; statutory elapsed timetables may be longer.
unknowns: Whether the assistant has formal supervisory authority.
Quality and ownership of current procedures and role profiles.
Employee representation arrangements and applicable national consultation requirements.
Which readiness assessments must be retained and for how long.
research_questions: Which procedures need supervised practice rather than simple acknowledgment?
Can existing permissions support a useful workload view without exposing unnecessary employee information?
new_work: Keep approved procedures, contacts and role mappings current.
Resolve missing or conflicting completion records.
Check that workload views do not become informal staff rankings.
Design and facilitate the first-month practice clinic.

tasks.short: Coordinate administrative projects and committee work, keeping plans, decisions and follow-up current.

steps.what: Agree objectives, responsibilities and limits with the project sponsor.
Create milestones, owners and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Chase task owners through the {EMAIL} for progress and blockers.
Copy received updates into the {PROJECT} and flag overdue work.
Discuss blockers, negotiate dependencies and agree actions during committee meetings.
Write minutes and circulate decisions and action owners through the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Meeting notes, explicit decisions and the attendee list.
loop.output: Draft minutes and actions with source references, owners and dates where stated.
loop.check: The assistant checks every decision against the notes; the chair approves circulation. Missing owners or dates remain flagged.
loop.stop: One draft per meeting; no automatic retries. Unclear decisions return to the chair for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion notes contain varied language; templates alone cannot reliably distinguish decisions from suggestions.

steps.what: Assemble the sponsor's status report from plans, actions and decisions.
Confirm deliverable acceptance and unresolved responsibilities with the sponsor.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} as the shared action register, with direct owner updates and scheduled reminders through the {WORKFLOW}, removing manual copying from the {EMAIL}. A bounded drafting loop turns meeting notes into minutes in the {DOCS}, with chair approval before circulation. A deterministic generator assembles dated status reports from the {PROJECT} and approved decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress lived in messages, plans and minutes, so the assistant repeatedly reconciled different versions. Interpreting discussion notes also required manual drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: Direct updates and scheduled reminders solve most coordination mechanically. A small, checked drafting loop can handle notes without delegating project decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Owners may not update records, dependencies can be political, and apparent agreement may conceal disagreement. A polished report cannot establish that work is complete.
tasks.human_edge: Surface disagreement, negotiate realistic commitments and judge when a blocker needs sponsor intervention.

ambition.what: Run a weekly cross-team dependency review before the monthly committee meeting.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time chasing and copying updates, and more time preparing dependency decisions. The sponsor can delegate escalation of overdue dependencies within agreed limits; scope, budget and acceptance rights remain with their current owners.

reach.task: Maintain a dependency and risk review for a small administrative project.
reach.learn: Critical dependencies, risk escalation and deliverable acceptance criteria.

evidence.claim: Meeting notes and minutes assistance are available today, supporting the feasibility of a bounded drafting step.
The departmental evaluation reported meeting-summary time savings and hallucinations; it does not establish this task's expected savings.
Direct task-owner updates, reminders and template-based status reports can use configured or deterministic technology.

assumptions: The assistant coordinates a small administrative project or participates in a committee, rather than directing a major programme.
Task owners enter structured status updates directly; interpreting arbitrary progress emails is outside the target design.
The model receives authorized meeting notes; recording and transcription are not required.
Reminders stop after two unanswered requests and place the item in the assistant's exception queue.
Status reports show source dates and missing updates rather than inventing progress.
GDPR applies to meeting records; national consultation requirements depend on actual employee-data use.
Build ranges are estimates for one project workspace and one minutes template.
unknowns: Whether task owners can and will maintain the shared register.
Existing project templates, committee approval practices and escalation rights.
Meeting-note sensitivity, permitted model processing and retention requirements.
Whether external committee members require restricted access.
research_questions: Which status fields are sufficient for sponsor decisions without creating extra reporting work?
How reliably can draft minutes distinguish agreed decisions from proposed actions on representative notes?
new_work: Review draft minutes and clarify missing decisions, owners or dates.
Handle non-response after the reminder limit.
Maintain templates, access controls and report mappings.
Check for stale updates and misleading status indicators.
Prepare and facilitate the weekly dependency review.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward payment exceptions, difficult arrangements, staff coaching and project dependencies. Explicit delegation can add dependency-escalation rights; spending, employment and project-acceptance authority do not expand automatically.
reach: Administrative services manager: review recurring service problems and improve administrative controls.
Project management specialist: prepare dependency reviews and evidence for acceptance decisions.
skills_to_grow: Source checking, GDPR-aware records handling and AI literacy.
role.ambitious_version: Coordinate a small administrative improvement programme that removes recurring service failures, while providing first-month practice support and earlier visibility of cross-team dependencies.

job.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
